summary.intent: Coordinate and verify several in-flight PRs in the caliper repo (convert single-flight #514, early-session reuse #515, heap-meter clamp #511), delegate a Callisto 0.22 config update to a worker, and check whether Rust and crate dependencies are up to date.
summary.outcome: Verified #514 (output identical to main on 5 corpora, Chakra CPU -10%, memory and determinism gates exit 0) and published its PR body. Recommended holding #515 because its 1-3% gain is within noise. Reported dependency status: Rust 1.99.1 vs 1.100.0, 82 lockfile updates, tsrs pinned at 0.24.0 vs 7.1.0-beta.tsrs4. The Callisto 0.22 worker is still running.

repo: Callisto config is confined to callisto.toml, .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml (pinned to 0.20.0 by SHA) and docs/releasing.md, so it can be delegated without colliding with workers on checker code.
Required gates for convert-style changes are `memory` and `determinism` via gate_harness; the gate fixture is built in scratch space outside the repo.
Lint/doc gate command set: `just lint doc-check machete typos` plus the full tests; semantic nextest is also used for verification.

The project pins tsrs crates (tsrs_api, tsrs_vfs, tsrs_core) exactly at =0.24.0 and sets rust-version = "1.99". Upstream tsrs now uses a new version scheme (7.1.0-beta.tsrsN) tracking the TypeScript 7.1 beta.
The weekly oracle run costs money, so running it requires user approval.
#512 and #513 are already merged, so main includes the private-name fix and the `declared` single-flight.
workflow: Lead agent verifies worker output itself (build, compare against main, gates, diff review) and records its own verification in the PR body before publishing.
Long gate runs go in a background script with a Monitor/task notification while other work such as diff review continues in parallel.
Independent work with disjoint file ownership is delegated to workers; the worker for Callisto must prove the 0.22 release plan equals the 0.20 plan before reporting.
Sequence dependency or toolchain bumps after in-flight checker PRs merge, and keep a tsrs spike separate from the Rust/cargo update so regressions can't hide.

friction: The convert worker skipped the memory and determinism gates, so the lead had to run them itself.
The convert build step was run twice before verification could proceed.
#515's measured gain (1-3%) is within noise and not reproducible, which makes the review conclusion weak.
The tsrs changelogs for the four newer releases haven't been read, so the risk of a breaking API change is unknown.
open_items: User decision needed on #511 (heap-meter clamp), #514 (convert single-flight, ready) and #515 (recommended hold).
Callisto 0.22 simplified-config worker is still running; its result must show the release plan matches 0.20.
Awaiting the user's go for the tsrs spike (read changelogs, try 7.1.0-beta.tsrs4 against the lane and corpora), pending the cost approval for the weekly oracle.
Rust 1.100.0 upgrade and `cargo update` (82 crates) as a separate low-risk change, to be started after #514 merges.
The modified files (callisto-release.yml, ci.yml, callisto.toml, docs/releasing.md) come from the Callisto worker and haven't been reviewed or reported on yet.
